sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: A set of AI agent skills from designer and engineer Emil Kowalski that help coding agents build better user interfaces, especially animations. They cover easing, timing, gestures, performance and design choices, based on his work at companies like Vercel and Linear.
sixtySeconds.problem: AI agents often pick the wrong details for UI motion, such as an ease-in curve on an enter animation, and small mistakes add up to an interface that feels off. These skills list those mistakes and how to fix them.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it to give your agent expert taste in motion and interface details, with skills for building, reviewing, auditing and removing animations.
requirements: An AI coding agent that supports skills

overview: The main skill, emil-design-eng, is mostly about animation with some design advice. Others build an animation from scratch (animate, animate-expo), review or improve existing ones, find or remove animation opportunities, coordinate several elements (choreograph) and fix dropped frames (animation-performance).

Further skills cover Apple-style design principles, 1:1 gestures, picking UI libraries, prototyping several versions of a component, making web apps feel native on phones, stress-testing UI with worst-case data, and learn-taste, which turns your corrections into rules in DESIGN.md.
Every skill has a page at aiforui.dev/skills with when to use it, an example result and prompts to try. The repository is MIT licensed.
